# ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ wins Oscar for best animated film

## ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ wins Oscar for best animated film

By JAMES POLLARD

Leer en español

“KPop Demon Hunters” won the Academy Award for best animated feature film on Sunday, capping a culturally defining run that has placed the musical-action movie atop both box-office and music charts.

Netflix’s big blockbuster follows HUNTR/X, a Korean girl group that battles otherworldly demons, a rival boy band and their lead singer’s own shame. Its choppy animation style, which combines 2D anime aesthetics with 3D CGI stylizations, underscores the high-octane action. The soundtrack, led by the Grammy-winning hit “Golden,” landed eight songs on the Billboard Hot 100. 'KPop Demon Hunters' Wins Oscar for Best Animated Movie 'KPop Demon Hunters' Wins Oscar for Best Animated Movie

It’s their moment!

“ KPop Demon Hunters” took home the Oscar for best animated feature at Sunday night’s Academy Awards. Netflix’s most-watched movie in history beat “Arco,” “Elio,” “Little Amélie or the Character of Rain” and “Zootopia 2” in the category.

The “KPop Demon Hunters” winning streak has been unstoppable. It won for best animated film at the Golden Globes, the Critics’ Choice Awards, PGA Awards and it took home 10 Annie Awards. The film, produced by Sony Animation, was directed by Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans, and produced by Michelle L.M. Wong. With the win, Kang and Wong make history as the first female Asian winners in best animated feature.

## Related Stories

### Margot Robbie, Mark Ruffalo, Daisy Ridley, Omar Sy Projects Lead Venice Immersive Lineup

During her acceptance speech, Kang said, “Thank you to the Academy and to all fans who got us here, and for those of you who look like me.” Tearfully, she said, “I’m so sorry that it took us so long to see us in a movie like this. But it is here. And that means that the next generations don’t have to go longing. This is for Korea and for Koreans everywhere.”

### Popular on Variety

A sequel was announced was week with Kang and Appelhans returning to direct and write the film, which is reportedly aiming for release in 2029. The follow-up film kicks off Appelhans and Kang’s new, exclusive multi-year writing and directing deal with Netflix across animation.

“Golden,” the breakout hit song from the film, also just won the Oscar for original song. It triumphed over “I Lied to You” from “ Sinners, Diane Warren’s “Dear Me” from her documentary “Diane Warren: Relentless,” Nick Cave and Bryce Dessner’s title song from “Train Dreams” and “Sweet Dreams of Joy” by Nicholas Pike from “Viva Verdi!”

“Golden” became the first K-pop song to ever to take home an Oscar. EJAE, who provides the singing voice of Rumi in the film, Mark Sonnenblick and South Korean hit factory the Black Label(Yu Han Lee, Hee Dong Nam, Zhun) made Oscar history by becoming the first Koreans to win best original song.

During her speech, a tearful EJAE said, “Growing up, people made fun of me liking KPop, but now everyone is singing our song and all of the Korean lyrics. I’m so proud. This award is not about success. It’s about resilience and I’m just so grateful to our team. I want to thank the resilient cast of ‘Demon Hunters.'”

Last month, EJAE spoke about how the film’s success had given her confidence to grow as a songwriter and as a Korean woman: “This film challenged me a lot in writing, singing, and really had to make me dig deep in my Korean side.”

She shared how creating work for this film was a healing journey. “I was dropped as a K-pop trainee as a kid and heard a lot of things about my singing voice, saying that it ‘was too low or kind of ugly.’ So while writing the songs, I was very ashamed of me being dropped and this movie allowed me to embrace that side. It was actually a superpower that hurt that I had, and the pain that I went through kind of helped me write the songs.”

Writing “Golden” helped her accept her voice and challenged her to sing and to be more confident. “This movie saved me to be honest.” She ended by saying, “It is just so beautiful and I feel so accepted. So thank you to the fans so much.”

The cast and creators of 'One Battle After Another' onstage after the pic's Best Picture Scar won Getty Images

Warner Bros’ action comedy One Battle After Another was named Best Picture at the 98th annual Academy Awards, which were handed out Sunday night at the Dolby Theater in Hollywood. See the full list below, followed by charts noting wins by film and by studio.

RELATED: All The Best Picture Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

RELATED: Oscars TV Review: Hollywood’s Big Night Finally Gets As Big As The Movies it Celebrates

One Battle After Another scored a leading six wins, and WB’s Depression-era genre smash Sinners was next with four, ending a marathon awards season in which the studio mates battled each other for months. Amid the studio’s $110 billion acquisition by Paramount Skydance, Warner Bros led distributors with 11 statuettes. Netflix was next with seven, including three for Frankenstein. The streamer’s KPop Demon Hunters was the only other film to score multiple trophies Sunday, and no other studio got more than one.

RELATED: The Oscars: Best Looks From The Red Carpet

RELATED: Oscars 2026: The Biggest Moments You Didn’t See On TV

RELATED: Oscars Analysis: In Changing Times This Was A Night Of Triumph For Original Filmmaking, Warner Bros, And A Hollywood On Edge

Michael B. Jordan won the contentious Best Actor race for his dual role as Smoke and Stack in Sinners, following up his triumph at the Actor Awards two weeks ago. It was his first career Academy Award nomination. Read more on his win from Deadline’s Baz Bamigboye here.

RELATED: All The Best Actor Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

Jessie Buckley then surprised no one with her Best Actress win for Focus Features’ Hamnet. She picked up her first career Oscar on her first nom and became the first Irishwoman to win the prize, after steamrolling through awards season for her aching portrayal of William Shakespeare’s partner Agnes.

RELATED: All The Best Actress Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

Paul Thomas Anderson took the statuette for Best Directing after winning earlier for Best Adapted Screenplay for One Battle After Another — his first Academy Awards after 11 previous nominations dating to 1998. He became just the ninth person to win Best Picture, Directing and Screenplay Oscars on the same night.

RELATED: Oscars 2026: What You Didn’t See On TV

Ryan Coogler followed with his first Oscar triumph, taking Original Screenplay for Sinners. It was his fifth career nomination. Anderson and Coogler also claimed the top screenplay prizes at the Writers Guild Awards. You can read the Sinners screenplay here.

RELATED: All The Best Director Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

One Battle After Another‘s Sean Penn won Best Supporting Actor, following up his win at the Actor Awards this month. It’s his third career Oscar but first in the category. He also has three other noms for Lead Actor. Penn wasn’t at the ceremony to accept his prize.

RELATED: All The Best Supporting Actor Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

After host Conan O’Brien’s monologue, Amy Madigan took home the first prize of the night, winning Best Supporting Actress for her role as creepy Aunt Gladys in Warner Bros’ Weapons. She was a favorite after winning at the Critics Choice and Actor Awards. Madigan also noted being a Supporting Actress Oscar nominee back in 1986 for Twice in a Life. Watch a video interview with Madigan here.

RELATED: All The Best Supporting Actress Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

The inaugural Oscar for Best Casting went to Cassandra Kulukundis of for One Battle After Another, who thanked those who “fought tirelessly” to get the category added. It was something of an upset in that the film was shut out at Casting Society’s Artios Awards in late February. The category’s nominees were announced one by one, honoring the award’s historic debut at the Academy Awards.

RELATED: Movies That Should Have Won The Best Picture Oscar – Photo Gallery

Netflix’s Frankenstein took three wins for craft awards, including two back-to-back for Best Makeup & Hairstyling and Best Costume Design. Guillermo del Toro‘s pic later won the statuette for Production Design. It also was a winner at the Make-Up Artists and Hair Stylists Guild Awards last month, taking that prize for Best Special Make-Up Prosthetics in Make-Up/Hairstyling. It also won for Excellence in Period Film at the CDGA and for Period Feature Film at the Art Directors Guild Awards. Watch a video interview with del Toro here.

RELATED: Snubs And Surprises At The 2026 Oscars: From Live-Action Short Film Tie To Films Leaving Empty-Handed

Also on the crafts front, Apple Original Films’ racing pic F1 took the Best Sound prize, Best Editing went to One Battle After Another, and Sinners won Best Cinematography. One Battle also was a winner at this year’s ACE Eddie Awards and ASC Awards. F1 took the checkered flag twice at Cinema Audio Society’s CAS Awards.

RELATED: All The Best International Feature Film Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

Norway picked up its first Academy Award ever with the Best International Feature win for Neon’s Cannes-debuting Sentimental Value. It also was up for Best Picture tonight. Javier Bardem presented the award, after he said “No to war, and free Palestine” onstage.

RELATED: The 60 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office

KPop Demon Hunters, Netflix’s most popular film ever, won the golden statuette for Best Animated Feature. The film produced by Sony Pictures Animation swept the Annie Awards last month, going 10-for-10 in its nominated categories. It has been streamed more than 500 million times, and its soundtrack has been streamed more than 11 billion times (with a capital B). See a gallery of the 25 highest-grossing animated movies of all time here.

RELATED: All The Best Animated Feature Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery

The pic later surprised no one by winning Best Song for the Grammy-winning international pop smash “Golden.” It’s the first tune from the K-pop genre to pick up an Oscar. That left Diane Warren with a record 17 career Oscar nominations without a win. She did pick up an Honorary Oscar at the 2022 Governor Awards, though.

20th Century Studios’ billion-dollar threequel Avatar: Fire and Ash won Best Visual Effects. It’s a sucker bet to pick against a pic in James Cameron’s historic franchise, which has taken FX Oscars for the original in 2010 and Avatar: The Way of Water in 2023. Fire and Ash dominated the VES Awards with seven wins last month.

RELATED: All 21 EGOT Winners From Rita Moreno to Whoopi Goldberg – Photo Gallery

In a major shocker, the Documentary Feature Oscar went to Mr. Nobody Against Putin, the Kino Lorber-distributed film that was Denmark’s entry for Best International Feature Film. The movie scooped the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award at Sundance last year, but the category was expected to be a race between favorites The Perfect Neighbor and Come See Me in the Good Light.

The Girl Who Cried Pearls got the win for Best Animated Short. Colm Feore narrates English-language version of the pic that debuted at last year’s Annecy International Film Festival. Later, The Singers (Netflix) and Two People Exchanging Saliva (Canal+/The New Yorker) both won for Live Action Short in only the seventh tie in Oscars history. All the Empty Rooms, about the fallout of school shootings, later won the Documentary Short prize.

RELATED: Where To Watch The 2026 Oscar Contenders, From ‘Sinners’ To ‘Sentimental Value’

Ludwig Göransson won his third career Oscar, Best Score for Sinners. He also was a winner at the Society of Composers and Lyricists’ SOC Awards. The Black Panther and Oppenheimer composer paid loving tribute to his father during his acceptance speech.

Billy Crystal began the lengthy In Memoriam segment with a tribute to his “best friend” Rob Reiner, who was killed along with his wife Michele in their home last year. Barbra Streisand paid heartfelt tribute to her late The Way We Were co-star Robert Redford and then sang a passage from its Oscar-winning theme song. There was a separate tribute to four female screen legends: Claudia Cardinale, Diane Ladd, Catherine O’Hara and Diane Keaton.

# ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ and ‘The Girl Who Cried Pearls’ Win the Best Animated Feature and Short Oscars

Ramin Zahed

By Ramin Zahed

March 15, 2026

As widely predicted, Sony Pictures Animation and Netflix’ record-breaking KPop Demon Hunters took home the Best Animated Oscar on Sunday. The Academy Award win for the animated feature, which continues to be Netflix’s most-watched movie, came on the heels of the movie winning all the other major animation awards of the year, including the Golden Globe for Best Animated Feature and 10 Annie Awards.

Directors Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans and producer Michelle Wong accepted the Oscar and thanked the Academy and their fans for the honor. “For those of you who look like me, I’m so sorry that it took us so long to see us in a movie like this,” said an emotional Kang. “That means, the next generation don’t have to go longing..this is for Korea and Koreans everywhere.”

“Music and stories have this power to connect us as humans across cultures and borders,” noted Appelhans. “I want to take a moment to tell young filmmakers, artists and musicians in all corners of the world, ‘Tell your stories, sing in your voice and, I promise you the world is waiting.”

KPop Demon Hunters’ ubiquitous “Golden” won the Best Song Oscar (Music and lyric by EJAE, Mark Sonnenblick, Joong Gyu Kwak, Yu Han Lee, Hee Dong Nam, Jeong Hoon Seo and Teddy Park) in a highly competitive category. First released in July, the song made history as the first K-pop song by a female act to top the Hot 100 since 2012, setting records for the animated group HUNTR/x (voices of EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and REI AMI).

KPop Demon Hunters, produced in partnership with Sony Pictures Animation, has reached more than 500 million views on Netflix since it debuted in June 2025. HUNTR/X is the first K-pop girl group to reach No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot 100, and “Golden” became the first K-pop song in history to win a Grammy Award. On Thursday, Netflix and Sony Pictures Animation officially announced that Kang and Appelhans will be directing the sequel to their blockbuster film.

The other nominees in this category were Arco, Elio, Little Amelie or the Character of Rain and Zootopia 2. While Disney and Pixar used to be regular winners in this category, Netflix, Sony Pictures Animation and indies like GKIDS and Janus Films/Sideshow have been become Academy favorites in recent years with titles such as Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, Miyazaki’s The Boy and the Heron, and Gints Zilbalodis’s Flow. The last time Disney won the Oscar in this category was five years ago when Jared Bush and Byron Howard’s Encanto took home the coveted prize.

National Film Board of Canada’s meticulously crafted stop-motion short, The Girl Who Cried Pearls, was the winner of the Best Animated Short Oscar. Directed by Chris Lavis and Maciek Sczerbowski, who were also nominated for their 2017 short Madame Tutli Putli, the short centers on a poor boy who falls in love with a girl whose sorrow turns into pearls at the dawn of the 20th century in Montreal. “I guess people think it takes patience to take five years to make a puppet film,” Lavis joked. “It actually takes patience to live with someone who takes five years to make a puppet film.” The filmmakers also thanked their home country of Canada and the city of Montreal for supporting their artistic efforts.”

The National Film Board of Canada has received the Oscar for Best Animated Short Film six times in the past: The Danish Poet (2006), Ryan (2004), Bob’s Birthday (1993), The Sand Castle (1977), and Special Delivery (1978). The other nominees in the category were Butterfly (Papillion), Forevergreen, Retirement Plan and The Three Sisters.

The Academy Award for Best Visual Effects went to James Cameron’s odds-on favorite Avatar: Fire and Ash. Camerons previous two trips to Pandora also received the VFX Oscar in 2010 and 2022. The four other nominees in this category were F1, Jurassic World Rebirth, The Lost Bus and Sinners. Receiving the award were Joe Letteri, Richard Baneham, Eric Sandron and Daniel Barrett.

# ‘One Battle After Another,’ ‘Sinners’ lead the way at 2026 Oscars: Complete list of winners

Paul Thomas Anderson's political thriller tallies six awards to four for Ryan Coogler's vampire musical. Michael B. Jordan, Jessie Buckley, Amy Madigan, and Sean Penn win the acting races.

### Marcus Errico

More stories by Marcus

Kevin Winter/Getty Images

Like so much of this season, the 2026 Oscars delivered one award after another to One Battle After Another, as Paul Thomas Anderson’s political opus led the way with six Academy Awards, including a triple play for PTA: Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Adapted Screenplay.

As expected, the 98th edition of Academy Awards was a back-and-forth showdown between One Battle and Sinners. Coming into Sunday, Ryan Coogler's vampire-musical mashup led the field with an unprecedented 16 nods, including Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor, Best Supporting Actress, and Best Supporting Actor. One Battle nearly matched with 13 nominations, going head-to-head with Sinners in each of those marquee categories. One Battle had the edge in the odds, having romped though the critics awards and precursors, but Sinners has a little bit of hoodoo that charmed Hollywood, providing plenty of suspense in one of the tightest races in years.

One Battle took an early lead with two milestone wins. An MIA Sean Penn scored Best Supporting Actor, becoming the eighth actor with three performance Oscars. And in an historic first, Cassandra Kulukundis won the inaugural Oscar for Best Casting in a surprise over Sinners' Francine Maisler. Then Anderson earned his first-career statuette for Best Adapted Screenplay and followed it up with Best Director and the final award of the night, Best Picture. The film also won film editing, as predicted.

Moments later, Coogler earned his first Oscar for Best Original Screenplay to get Sinners on the board. Composer Ludwig Göransson added Best Score to the Sinners register later in the show. And director of photography Autumn Durald Arkapaw scored a historic win for Best Cinematography, becoming the first woman and Black person to win that category. Michael B. Jordan capped the big Sinners evening by winning Best Actor.

Jessie Buckley completed her season sweep with the Best Actress Oscar for Hamnet. Amy Madigan scored the opening statuette of the night, winning Best Supporting Actress for her instantly iconic role as Aunt Gladys in Weapons.

Frankenstein picked up a trio of statuettes for Costume Design, Makeup and Hairstyling, and Production Design, while KPop Demon Hunters doubled up, with wins for Best Animated Feature and Best Song for "Golden."

Sentimental Value won Best International Feature, while Mr. Nobody Against Putin was named Best Documentary Feature.

Finally, in another one for the record books, there was a tie for Best Live-Action Short — only the seventh time ever— between "The Singers" and "Two People Exchanging Saliva."

Conan O'Brien hosted the ceremony from Hollywood's Dolby Theatre for the second straight year.
